stem: A bacterial capsular polysaccharide undergoes covalent linkage in a conjugate vaccine. Which of the following immune changes is the main purpose of this linkage?

options.label: A
options.text: Delivery of preformed pathogen-specific serum antibody
options.misconception: Confuses antigen conjugation with passive delivery of an already formed antibody.
options.explanation: Covalent linkage changes how the polysaccharide antigen elicits immunity; the cited mechanism is not delivery of preformed serum antibody.

options.label: B
options.text: Preservation of a T-cell-independent immune response
options.misconception: Keeps the original response type instead of recognizing the conversion produced by conjugation.
options.explanation: The source describes the opposite change: covalent linkage converts the polysaccharide antigen from T-cell independent to T-cell dependent.

options.label: C
options.text: Conversion to a T-cell-dependent immune response
options.misconception: None; covalent linkage converts the polysaccharide response to T-cell dependence and supports long-term immunity.
options.explanation: The FDA passage states that covalent linkage makes an otherwise T-cell-independent polysaccharide antigen T-cell dependent, inducing long-term immunity.

options.label: D
options.text: Suppression of polysaccharide recognition by lymphocytes
options.misconception: Treats covalent linkage as a way to mask the antigen rather than change the immune response.
options.explanation: The FDA passage describes conversion to a durable T-cell-dependent response, not suppression of recognition of the polysaccharide antigen.

options.label: E
options.text: Replication of a live organism after administration
options.misconception: Imports the defining step of a live vaccine into a chemically linked antigen preparation.
options.explanation: The cited mechanism is covalent linkage and conversion of response type; it does not require a live organism to replicate after administration.

context: Learning objective: explain the immune effect of covalent linkage in a conjugate vaccine. The linkage turns an otherwise T-cell-independent polysaccharide response into a T-cell-dependent one, inducing long-term immunity.
